problems.stem: You finished a CAT 100 essay. Which file name will still tell you what it is in three weeks?
options: final.docx
document(2).docx
2026-05-28_cat100_essay_v3.docx
asdf.docx
problems.explanation: A name with date, course, task, and version (2026-05-28_cat100_essay_v3.docx) stays readable. 'final' and 'document(2)' lose meaning once a fourth version appears.

problems.stem: Which folder structure keeps one assignment's files together and easy to find?
options: All coursework saved loose on the Desktop
CAT100 / Module07 / file-organization / (essay, notes, rubric inside)
One Downloads folder shared by every class
An Images folder holding photos from all five courses
problems.explanation: A course-then-module-then-task tree keeps related files in one place. Desktop dumps and type-based folders scatter a single task.

problems.stem: Your only copy of a paper lives on a USB stick that just stopped mounting. What practice would have prevented losing the work?
options: Renaming the file to FINAL before the deadline
Keeping two copies in two places, such as local plus OneDrive
Saving the file as a PDF instead of a DOCX
Storing the file in a deeper subfolder
problems.explanation: A two-copies-two-places rule survives a single drive failure. File format, depth, and a rename do nothing against a dead drive.

problems.stem: You have lab1.pdf, lab2.pdf, and slides.pptx for one module. A classmate suggests an 'All PDFs' folder. Why is grouping by task usually better here?
options: PDFs and PPTX files cannot share a folder
Grouping by task keeps the whole module together so nothing is hunted across type folders
PowerPoint files must always sit on the Desktop
File type folders load faster than task folders
problems.explanation: The lab PDFs and the slides belong to one module, so a task folder keeps them together. Type folders split one assignment across the disk.

problems.stem: An AI organize-my-folder tool (such as Copilot Suggested Rename or File Explorer AI Actions) proposes renaming your CAT 100 folder to a date-leading scheme, padding versions as _v2, and auto-deleting files it labels 'duplicates.' Which response shows a bounded AI move?
options: Accept everything, since the AI has read the file contents
Reject everything, since AI tools cannot help with file organization
Accept the date-leading pattern, modify the version padding to _v02, and reject the auto-delete because the tool cannot know which version has the corrected calculations
Accept the auto-delete first so the folder is smaller before renaming
problems.explanation: A bounded move accepts what fits your convention, modifies what is close, and rejects what you cannot verify. Auto-deleting 'duplicates' is the unverifiable step: the AI cannot tell which copy holds the corrected calculations.
